paragraphs.title: The Removal of Supports and the Collapse of Leadership

answers: The stay and staff of bread and water, along with their leaders
Their walls and gates
Their vineyards and houses
easy.explanation: The Lord takes away the stay and staff, including bread and water, as well as many kinds of leaders.
easy.q: What does the Lord take away from Jerusalem and Judah at the beginning of the passage?

answers: The ancient and the prophets
Children and babes
The mighty men and men of war
easy.explanation: The passage says, “I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them.”
easy.q: Who will rule in place of capable leaders?

answers: That he does not know the city
That he does not want to speak to the people
That he cannot be a ruler because he has neither bread nor clothing
easy.explanation: He says, “In my house is neither bread nor clothing,” and refuses to rule the people.
easy.q: What does the man say when he is asked to become a ruler?

answers: Both show the loss of basic necessities and stable leadership
Both describe economic prosperity and military success
Both refer only to changes in clothing
medium.explanation: The passage describes the removal of both essential supplies and capable leaders.
medium.q: What is the connection between taking away bread and water and the collapse of leadership?

answers: A weapon of war
A support or something on which people depend
A ruler’s garment
medium.explanation: A stay is a support, and here it refers especially to the support provided by bread and water.
medium.q: What does the word “stay” mean in this passage?

answers: He does not know the elders
He wants the children to rule
He feels that he does not even have basic necessities
medium.explanation: He explains that his house has neither bread nor clothing, so he cannot take responsibility for the people.
medium.q: Why does the man refuse to accept authority?

answers: Supports are removed, unfit rulers arise, and people refuse responsibility
There is first abundance, then good leaders, and finally a rebuilt city
The warriors fall, ornaments are removed, and water appears
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the removal of support and leadership to childish rule and refusal to accept authority.
challenge.q: What progression is described in the passage?

answers: The normal social order and patterns of respect are overturned
Children become wiser than all the ancient people
The ancient willingly give away all their possessions
challenge.explanation: The description shows the young and dishonourable treating the old and respected with arrogance.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the child behaving proudly against the ancient and the base against the honourable?

answers: It shows that the man wants to build a new house
It emphasizes that he views public responsibility as a burden he lacks the means to bear
It shows that he has only a family position, not a public one
challenge.explanation: The man points to the condition of his household to explain why he cannot become a ruler.
challenge.q: Why is the reference to the “house of his father” important in the request for leadership?

paragraphs.title: Sin, Judgment, and Injustice Toward the Poor

answers: Because their tongue and their doings are against the Lord
Because they have no clothing
Because the children refuse to eat bread
easy.explanation: The passage connects their fall with their words and actions against the Lord.
easy.q: Why are Jerusalem and Judah fallen according to the passage?

answers: As hidden sin that no one knows
As sin that no longer exists
As open sin that they do not hide
easy.explanation: They “declare their sin as Sodom” and “hide it not.”

answers: The ancient people and the princes
The children only
The poor of the city
easy.explanation: The Lord enters into judgment with the ancient people and their princes.
easy.q: Against whom will the Lord enter into judgment?

answers: A field of trees
A place where grapevines are grown
A gate of the city
medium.explanation: A vineyard is a cultivated place where grapevines grow.

answers: They oppressed the people and harmed the poor
They refused to wear clothing
They removed bread and water from their own houses
medium.explanation: The Lord asks why they beat His people to pieces and grind the faces of the poor.
medium.q: What injustice is charged against the leaders in verse 15?

answers: Both describe leaders abusing their power
Both describe two kinds of celebration
Both concern only the appearance of the city
medium.explanation: The passage condemns the leaders for causing the people to err and for oppressing the poor.
medium.q: What is the connection between misleading the people and mistreating the poor?

answers: Their sin is open, notorious, and boldly displayed
The people willingly left Jerusalem
Their sin is connected only with drought
challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes that their sin is public and not concealed.
challenge.q: What is the meaning of comparing their sin to the sin of Sodom?

answers: They are responsible for leading the people and directing public affairs
They are the only people left in the city
They were responsible for making ornaments
challenge.explanation: The leaders are held accountable for misleading the people, spoiling the vineyard, and oppressing the poor.
challenge.q: Why is judgment directed especially toward the ancient people and the princes?

answers: Poverty was caused only by a lack of rain
The leaders enjoyed in their homes what had been taken unjustly from the poor
The poor built houses for the princes
challenge.explanation: The phrase suggests that the leaders possessed the results of their exploitation of the poor.
challenge.q: What does “the spoil of the poor is in your houses” suggest?

paragraphs.title: The Pride of the Daughters of Zion and the Removal of Their Ornaments

answers: War and building walls
Beauty, ornaments, and attracting attention
Working in vineyards and distributing bread
easy.explanation: They are described as haughty, adorned, and eager to draw attention to themselves.
easy.q: What are the daughters of Zion focused on in this passage?

answers: Add more ornaments to them
Build houses for them
Take away their ornaments and signs of beauty
easy.explanation: The Lord will remove their tinkling ornaments, clothing, jewelry, and other adornments.
easy.q: What will the Lord do in that day?

answers: Sackcloth, baldness, and humiliation
Bread, water, and fine clothing
Crowns, rings, and songs
easy.explanation: The passage contrasts beauty with baldness, sackcloth, burning, and other signs of judgment.
easy.q: What will replace beauty and adornment?

answers: Walking in an affected or showy manner
Sitting on the ground in mourning
Hiding their faces
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a deliberately noticeable and affected way of walking.
medium.q: What does “mincing as they go” describe?

answers: Showy concern with beauty is replaced by humiliation and loss
Concern with beauty leads to receiving more ornaments
The behavior has no connection to the judgment
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts prideful display with the removal of adornments and the coming disgrace.
medium.q: What is the connection between the behavior in verse 16 and the judgment in verses 17–24?

answers: The extent of the people’s concern with outward appearance
That all the ornaments were weapons
That the women had left Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The detailed list highlights how extensively their lives were centered on adornment.
medium.q: What does the long list of ornaments and garments emphasize?

answers: A change from luxury and attention to humiliation, loss, and mourning
A change from war to peace
A change from poverty to wealth
challenge.explanation: The passage places symbols of beauty and luxury against signs of judgment and disgrace.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between sweet smell, beauty, and fine clothing and the results listed afterward?

answers: It shows that the removal will be comprehensive, not limited to one item
It proves that all the ornaments were instruments of war
It describes the rebuilding of the city
challenge.explanation: Because many articles are listed, their removal represents a complete reversal of the former lifestyle.
challenge.q: Why does the long list of ornaments strengthen the meaning of the judgment?

answers: Beauty will remain despite the judgment
Beauty will be replaced by injury, disgrace, and destruction
Beauty will become a symbol of victory
challenge.explanation: The phrase summarizes the replacement of outward beauty with painful and humiliating consequences.
challenge.q: What does “burning instead of beauty” mean in context?

paragraphs.title: The Fall of the Men and the Mourning of Jerusalem

answers: By the sword and in war
By hunger alone
Because their ornaments are removed
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war.”
easy.q: How will the men of Zion fall?

answers: Rejoice and open widely
Lament and mourn
Put on fine garments
easy.explanation: The gates are poetically described as lamenting and mourning.

answers: It will expand and become full
It will sit upon the ground in desolation
It will replace its rulers
easy.explanation: Jerusalem is described as desolate and sitting upon the ground.
easy.q: What will happen to Jerusalem at the end of the passage?

answers: The men’s deaths in war lead to emptiness and mourning in Jerusalem
The city’s mourning causes the men to go to war
There is no connection between the two descriptions
medium.explanation: The fall of the men produces the city’s desolation, lamentation, and grief.
medium.q: What is the connection between the fall of the men and the mourning of the city?

answers: Prosperity and independence
Humiliation, desolation, and mourning
Celebration after victory
medium.explanation: Sitting on the ground expresses a low and mournful condition.
medium.q: What does Jerusalem sitting upon the ground symbolize?

answers: Empty and forsaken
Newly decorated
Rebuilt and prosperous
medium.explanation: Desolate means empty, deserted, or forsaken.
medium.q: What does “desolate” mean in this passage?

answers: It shows the practical results of sin and judgment: death, emptiness, and mourning
It cancels all the warnings given earlier
It restores Jerusalem to its former glory
challenge.explanation: The final verses gather together the consequences of judgment upon the people and the city.
challenge.q: How does the ending complete the chapter’s message of judgment?

answers: The mourning affects the whole city, not only individuals
Only the gates were harmed, while the people were safe
The city is portrayed as a place of celebration
challenge.explanation: By describing the gates as mourning, the passage presents the entire city as sharing in the grief.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the gates of the city being described as mourning?

answers: The men fall in war, the gates mourn, and Jerusalem sits desolate on the ground
The women adorn themselves, the vineyard is restored, and rulers rise
Children appear, water is distributed, and the city prospers
challenge.explanation: The verses move from the fall of the men to the mourning and desolation of Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in verses 25–26?
